json_schema.description: An existing metadata record about a dataset, as a repository or catalogue holds it. The input a quality or validation agent assesses. Slots are the DCAT and Dublin Core terms a minimal record carries; TODO(#22): widen when a real repository export is exercised.

identifier.description: The record's own identifier, e.g. a DOI or a catalogue URI.

licence.description: The licence the record declares, as an IRI or SPDX identifier.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

criterion.description: The quality criterion assessed, e.g. licence_present.

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).

message.description: The finding, as a sentence a reviewer can act on.

GroundingRef.description: The identity and content hash of one retrieved thing a payload rests on. The only way a payload may name an external resource as a decided identity, and the only place it names it: what the reference identifies is read from the evidence item with the same source_id and content_hash (docs/specs/grounding.md). The linter matches every GroundingRef against a retrieval span on both fields.

json_schema.$comment: Generated from data_director.yaml by `uv run dd-gen-schema`. Do not edit.

ChoiceAnswer.description: The researcher's answer to the choice question the turn before asked: the values they chose and any text they gave in place of an option. The app checks it against that question before it sends the turn (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

answer_other.description: The researcher's own answer, given in place of an option where the question allows it.

answer_to.description: The invocation whose reply asked the question.

answer_values.description: The values of the options chosen; empty when the researcher answered in their own words.

ChoiceAnswer.title: ChoiceAnswer

ConversationTurn.description: One earlier turn of a conversation, as the caller presents it to the agent. An agent turn names the agent and version that produced it and the invocation it came from.

turn_agent_id.description: For an agent turn, the agent that produced it.

turn_agent_version.description: For an agent turn, the version of the agent that produced it.

turn_invocation_id.description: For an agent turn, the invocation it came from.

turn_text.description: What was said in the turn.

ConversationTurn.title: ConversationTurn

InventorySummary.description: What the inventory a project holds is, without its files: the conductor fills it into a Message so that the agent knows the project has one (docs/specs/projects.md).

inventory_digest.description: The inventory's dd-input-json-v1 hash, by which the project keeps it.

inventory_file_count.description: How many files the inventory lists.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

InventorySummary.title: InventorySummary

StepProgress.description: How far one step of the Blueprint's process flow has gone, as the project log shows it: started, done or skipped. A step the list leaves out is open (docs/specs/orchestration.md).
StepProgress.title: StepProgress

StepState.description: How far a process-flow step has gone; a step with none of these states is open.
StepState.title: StepState

TurnRole.description: Who spoke in a conversation turn.
TurnRole.title: TurnRole

json_schema.description: One conversational turn addressed to an agent: the text of the turn and the conversation so far. The history is part of the input, so the input hash covers everything the agent saw. In a project that holds an inventory, the conductor adds what it is (docs/specs/projects.md); in any project, it adds the entry point chosen, the progress the project log shows and the project's title, if it has one (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

choice_answer.description: The researcher's answer to the choice question the previous turn asked, when they answered by choosing. message_text still carries the answer as prose.

history.description: The earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first.

message_text.description: What the user said in this turn.

project_entry.description: The Blueprint entry point (1, 2 or 3) the researcher chose for the conversation's project, the latest chosen. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or none was chosen.

project_inventory.description: The inventory the conversation's project holds, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds no inventory.

project_progress.description: The process-flow steps the conversation's project log shows started, done or skipped, in flow order. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project. Derived from the log on every turn, never stored.

project_title.description: The conversation's project's latest title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or the project has no title yet.

project_title_by_researcher.description: Whether a person gave the project its title, so that a model's would be refused; false while the project has no title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

json_schema.title: Message
